news.title: Chelsea Women's starting line up vs Liverpool confirmed
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made two changes to her Chelsea side for today’s Women’s Super League clash against Liverpool. After picking up a late win against Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Women’s Champions League on Wednesday, the focus turns to extending our lead at the top of the table in the last game before the international break. Bompastor has made two changes to the team as Lucy Bronze returns to the side, replacing Nathalie Bjorn in defence. The other change in the starting line-up comes as Sjoeke Nusken replaces Aggie Beever-Jones. Meanwhile, Manaka Matsukubo is fit enough to return to the substitutes' bench after missing the midweek game against PSG. news.title: Alonso underlines importance of control on and off the ball
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has highlighted Chelsea’s ability to control the game, both when in and out of possession, as key to our chances of victory against Leeds United, as well as the games which follow. The Blues host Leeds at Stamford Bridge at 3pm this afternoon, as we return to Premier League action following the last international break of the year. Giving his thoughts on today’s game and what his team needs to do to secure all three points, one aspect was clearly high in his mind, underlining a key aspect he has been working on with his players at Cobham. ‘We have had spells with control, other spells that I would like us to have better control,’ Alonso explained. ‘I'm not meaning just control with the ball. Sometimes you can have control without the ball because things are going the way you have planned. You feel comfortable that “okay we don't have the ball, but we know what we are doing”. ‘When you have an idea where you feel comfortable that the opponent has the ball and where you don't feel comfortable that the opponent has the ball, and when you know that they have the ball where you want them to have it, you can feel good control of the game. ‘It's something that's in my mind, because that's the way I like to play, but we are working for that to get better.’ Control could also be particularly important against a Leeds side who seems to relish the physical aspects of the game and exploiting the loose-ball situations that result from them. No team in the Premier League has won as many individual duels as the Whites this season. However, Alonso is reluctant to view that as a purely physical or mental challenge. He sees everything in football as being linked, with the issue of control again at the forefront, but admits it is an obstacle his players will need to overcome. ‘First of all, it's the Premier League. It's not just against Leeds, that will happen next week against Forest, and the next one against Palace. This is the level of the competition and we know how important it can be,’ said our manager. ‘It's not just the duels. It's about the football things or the tactical things. When you have good control, normally you are in better positions to face duels. When you don't have that much control, you are not in that good position. ‘So it's not just about going one-v-one and let's see what happens. No, I think that you can help situations, to be stronger in the duels. After, for sure, it's the individual qualities that help a lot, but you can help as well. ‘It's also tactical things. Because for me, everything comes with, for sure, the mentality, but many things are down to the football reasons. When we analyse we can talk about lacking intensity, but why did we lack intensity? Why didn't we press well? Why were the distances there? What did we or didn't we do in the trigger moments or trying to squeeze? ‘So mainly I focus on the football things because I think that if that works, in the mental things it helps the players.’ The Blues will no doubt be tested physically and mentally when we return to the pitch in the highly competitive surroundings of the Premier League this afternoon, but Alonso seems confident his team can pass with flying colours.

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds Utd | Primed for battle at the Bridge
Bompastor highlights Cuthbert's importance ahead of 'difficult' Liverpool test
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has underlined Erin Cuthbert’s importance to Chelsea as the club captain targets a return to the starting XI for our Women’s Super League clash against Liverpool. Cuthbert has appeared as a substitute in our last three games, and Bompastor stated that a knock suffered in the draw against Hacken prevented her from starting the win against title rivals Manchester City. The Blues coach added that Cuthbert is now back fit enough to be competing for a starting role, but admitted that the competition for places is currently fierce because of the performances from her team-mates. ‘I always talk to my players and give them the reality in terms of where they are in terms of the performances,’ Bompastor said. ‘So when we started this block we had a really good conversation with Erin saying to her what our ambitions for the block were and the plan. ‘I think probably when she got that knock against Hacken at the end of the game, she made a little step back and the plan was for her to be able to start the Man City game but she couldn't - I think she was not 100 per cent for that game. ‘After the scenario of the game when the substitutions didn't help, right now she's not far from starting games. I think she's fit enough to be able do that, but the team is performing at a really good level. ‘I'm also really happy with the performances from the other players who are playing right now. So she knows what she needs to do and she's an important player for us. ‘Going into the game we will need to bring some energy, some fresh legs; she didn't play much [against PSG] so she will be probably fresh and ready to start if she has to.’ Asked whether her team might need the ‘bite’ that Cuthbert brings for the battle against Liverpool, Bompastor admitted that she hadn’t yet made a decision on her starters for Saturday - but highlighted the midfielder’s importance to the team and the different aspects she could bring to some team-mates. '[It could be] a good game for her to play. Again, she's a really important player for us,’ Bompastor said. ‘She's our captain, she brings a lot of quality. ‘When she's on the pitch, she's a different profile from some of the players who are playing right now. I will analyse Liverpool again and see what is the most appropriate for us to start the game with and maybe bringing also an impact from the bench.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds: All you need to know
news.body_en: An age-old, long-distance rivalry is rekindled at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton preview the 99th instalment of northern grit versus King’s Road swagger at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea host Leeds United just ten weeks after the Yorkshiremen’s recent cup visit. The Blues delivered a thrilling 6-3 victory over the Whites in that Carabao Cup encounter and the visitors have not won at the Bridge on any front for more than a quarter of a century. However, before the international break, Leeds beat Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 for their first three-point haul since September. They stand ninth in the table, while the Londoners slipped to fifth after defeat at Sunderland by the same score. Xabi Alonso’s side also rank fifth for points gained on home soil this season, while Daniel Farke’s men are 11th-best on the road. Last season, this fixture finished 2-2, the Blues having led 2-0 until well past the hour mark. We also won 1-0 in the FA Cup to make it ten unbeaten against the Yorkshiremen. Chelsea are already eight points better off than in the corresponding ten fixtures last season and could return to fourth place with a win. The good news from Alonso’s pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon was that Josh Acheampong, Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez are all available to feature against Leeds following the international break. ‘Moises is ready to start,’ our manager confirmed. ‘It was discussed after playing the first game [for Ecuador] he could save some minutes. That was good for him, and he’s fine.’ ‘Emi is in the squad and he is selectable. Against Sunderland two weeks ago probably there was risk, and the plan was for him to train more with Argentina and to play one game. It went well so he’s available.’ However, Jamie Gittens, Jorrel Hato, Reece James, Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix all remain out of contention as they continue to work on their recovery at Cobham. ‘Joao’s not yet fit to train with the team. We need to wait a bit more. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see day-by-day how he is feeling. ‘Jorrel has a back problem. We need to be patient because it’s going to take a while.’ Though they were played on neutral soil, the epic 1970 final battles between Chelsea and Leeds, in pursuit of an FA Cup neither ha won at the time, are always mentioned in regard to this fixture. For those who witnessed the 2-2 at Wembley and the Blues’ stunning victory thanks to David Webb’s header at Old Trafford, the intrigue, culture clash, violence and satisfying conclusion were unforgettable. They established the tone for relations between the two camps for generations. The Whites most recently returned to the top flight in 2025 and the Blues had won every visit during their previous three-season tenancy between 2020 and 2023. In the Covid-restricted meeting in December 2020, attended by 2,000 at the Bridge, Cobham graduate Patrick Bamford broke the deadlock, but Marco Bielsa’s side saw Oliver Giroud restore parity, then Kurt Zouma and Christian Pulisic deliver a 3-1win. History repeated itself the following year, with Leeds edging ahead through a penalty, before Mason Mount levelled. After the interval, Jorginho put the European champions ahead, also from 12 yards. The Yorkshiremen equalised with seven minutes remaining, but at the death a rare second spot-kick conversion by Jorginho settled the game at 3-2. Wesley Fofana’s first league goal for Chelsea was enough to claim the points in March 2023, a few months before Javi Gracia’s side were relegated. Last February, Leeds came back from goals by Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer to draw 2-2, scoring with their only shots on target. Chelsea’s tally of 13 Premier League goals on home soil has been bettered only by Brighton (15). The Blues have recorded the highest shot accuracy in the top flight this season – 41.9 per cent. Between the international breaks, the Blues conceded one goal from open play, two from corners and two penalties. Nottingham Forest (nine) and Sunderland (eight) are the only top-flight clubs to have scored fewer goals so far than Leeds (ten). The Whites have opened the scoring in three of their five away league matches. Mike Penders, honoured for last month’s finger-tip save against Man Utd, is Chelsea’s first recipient of the Premier League Save of the Month award since Robert Sanchez in October 2024, and our fourth ever. news.title: Latest update on James and Lacroix returns from Alonso
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso discussed the chances of Reece James and Maxence Lacroix getting back on the pitch before the end of the year, as the pair continue their recovery from injury. Both players have been absent in recent weeks - our captain James after undergoing minor knee surgery, centre-back Lacroix due to a hamstring issue. The duo are working hard to get back in the action with Chelsea as soon as possible, but Alonso had already confirmed that our next fixture against Leeds United on Saturday will be too soon for either of them to be involved. The Spaniard has now provided further clarity around hopes that James and Lacroix could be back out on the pitch for the Blues before the end of 2026. ‘I think that Max has a better chance than Reece,’ our manager revealed. ‘It’s not definitely that Reece won’t be back before then, but Max has a better chance.’ James and Lacroix have been important figures in Alonso’s team, starting all but one of the Premier League matches they have been available for. Just like Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo, who have missed games in recent weeks, their absence would be a blow for any team. However, the Chelsea manager knows that injuries are an unavoidable part of football, and insists it is up to him and the other players to be ready to find solutions on the pitch. ‘We want to have a complete squad, for sure. That's the goal of any manager,’ added Alonso. ‘We have built a good squad, knowing that some players, they have this experience, they have this role, they have this specificity that is very needed, and we are a better team with them. ‘But it's not about making a big drama when someone gets injured, because that happens. So we need to deal with that. ‘We need to find the other players that are available. They need to show that they are good enough, and that's our dynamic.’ Those selected in Alonso’s next starting line-up will be looking to do just that when we host Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for a 3pm kick-off on Saturday. news.title: Penders reflects on PL Save of the Month
Alonso says Blues are ‘building an identity’ but need consistency
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes his Chelsea side are well on their way to forming the ‘identity’ he wants to see from them, even though he knows it is a process that takes time. Alonso arrived this summer, since when the Blues have had some standout results, such as the thrilling home wins over Brighton and Bournemouth. The manager recognises the next step is consistency. Developing the character of the team in order to be competitive on a regular basis is his aim. ‘We are building it,’ Alonso said on his team’s identity. ‘I think that this is a process. ‘The goal for us is that we feel that this is our idea of how we want to play, knowing the context, knowing the Premier League, but that we are prepared with whoever we are facing, and that we are competitive. ‘We want to be competitive, and that's the goal. We are lacking a bit of consistency on the results for sure. We have won some games, but had some defeats as well, and we are in that process to get better. It will take a while.’ Leeds provide stiff opposition in our first game back after the international break. Alonso is acutely aware of how tough they are to play against both physically and tactically. They have conceded just eight goals in ten games, and have only been beaten twice. ‘We know that nowadays you need to be flexible each game, even during the game, that one structure can change with the ball, without the ball,’ Alonso said. ‘Leeds are a demanding team, not just physically, tactically as well. They are doing great things with the manager they have. They have been together, so they have a pretty clear idea, and it's going to be a very demanding game.' Alonso added exactly what he wants from his players as they look to get back to winning ways at Stamford Bridge. ‘We need to work,' he said. 'We need to be patient. We need to be intense. We need to have a good concentration and focus, and to know that each detail can be very important.’ There's still time to secure your place for Chelsea v Leeds at Stamford Bridge. news.title: Cobham Unseen: pre-Leeds Utd (h)
Training gallery: Blues make last preparations for Leeds
Alonso: Emegha and Welbeck ready to offer Blues alternative
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck are both ready to play their part against Leeds in the absence of Joao Pedro in attack. The Brazilian striker has missed the last four games through injury, and Alonso confirmed that Chelsea’s No.9 would not be back in time for this weekend’s Premier League clash, our first since the final international break of 2026. Emegha and Welbeck both arrived at Stamford Bridge this summer, and have largely featured from the bench so far. Alonso says both are capable of stepping into the fold in attack, and can offer different strengths as alternatives in Joao Pedro’s absence. ‘They are both ready,’ Alonso said at his press conference on Friday afternoon. ‘Both different qualities, different stages of a career. Danny has played so many games, he has great experience, he has quality. And Eme, he has this power, this physicality. He's waiting for the chance, and we have enough games to try. ‘It's not just the strikers who can score,’ added Alonso. ‘We need the whole team for that. We can score in set-pieces from defenders, midfielders. So it's teamwork, for sure. ‘Joao is an important player, but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options, and we need to keep trying.’ Alonso also praised Mike Penders for the way he adapted to replacing Emiliano Martinez in goal. The young Belgian started games after Martinez suffered a nasty jaw injury away at Everton in October. Following an individual error in the defeat to Tottenham, Alonso was pleased to see the 21-year-old’s reaction, commending him for the progress he has made in a short space of time. ‘Mike has done very good things,’ Alonso said. ‘I think that we know the progression that he had, that he overcame a difficult moment for sure after the first game. But after he's done better. ‘He's improving, and with his minutes, his development has been good.’

news.title: Club statement
news.body_en: Chelsea FC can confirm the club has been fined by The Football Association following a charge of misconduct in relation to the FA Cup away fixture at Charlton Athletic on Saturday 10 January 2026. An independent Regulatory Commission has imposed a £150,000 fine, an action plan and a warning regarding the future conduct of supporters following abusive, offensive and discriminatory chanting. We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club. Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this. Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary. Discriminatory behaviour may constitute a criminal offence and supporters found to have breached the club’s regulations will face disciplinary action, including possible match bans or membership suspensions. We will also require all those who may be sanctioned to take part in the Kick it Out programme as we believe education is as important as sanctions in order to root out this behaviour for good. We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward. news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Leeds
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has provided an update on the fitness of several members of his Chelsea squad, including Joao Pedro, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Moises Caicedo, Emiliano Martinez and Jorrel Hato. He also reported the latest on longer-term absentees Reece James and Jamie Gittens. The Blues are back in action this weekend following the final international break of 2026. We host Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, hoping to return to winning ways after losing at Sunderland last time out. Alonso confirmed he will not be able to call upon the services of Joao Pedro, who hasn’t played since the win at Everton last month because of a thigh issue. ‘He’s not yet fit to train with the team,’ said Alonso. ‘We need to wait a bit more. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see day by day how he is feeling.’ Alonso said Lacroix, who has a hamstring problem, is in a ‘similar situation’ to the Brazilian striker and will not be able to feature against Leeds. The manager also ruled Hato out. He said: ‘Jorrel has a back problem. We need to be patient because it’s going to take a while.’ There was better news regarding Acheampong and Caicedo. Acheampong didn’t play for England Under-21s during the international break, while Caicedo came off at half-time in Ecuador’s most recent friendly. ‘Moises is ready to start. It was discussed after playing the first game he could save some minutes. That was good for him, and he’s fine.’ Alonso replied with an affirmative ‘yes’ when asked if Acheampong can return to action, while he also provided an update on Martinez, who represented his country during the international break. ‘He is in the squad and he is selectable,’ said Alonso. ‘Against Sunderland two weeks ago probably there was risk, and the plan was for him to train more with Argentina and to play one game. It went well so he’s available for tomorrow.’ Alonso’s final fitness news regarded James and Gittens, who have not played for us since September. ‘Reece is getting there. He’s taking a step forward, but still needs some weeks. ‘Jamie Gittens is better,’ added Alonso. ‘He’s already training with the team, but we want to give him more time until he comes back in the squad.’ There's still time to secure your place for Chelsea v Leeds at Stamford Bridge. news.title: Made in Cobham: Andrew Pennie
news.body_en: From a football-mad childhood to growing up at Chelsea, Andrew Pennie reflects on the people, experiences and lessons that have shaped him on and off the pitch, fresh from signing his first professional contract with the Blues. For most of Andrew Pennie's life, football and Chelsea have been constants – and both have shaped the player and person he is today. Growing up in Lewisham with two older brothers, there was rarely a quiet moment in the Pennie house. Our young forward remembers playing EA FC [then known as FIFA] with his siblings and naturally claims he was the best. The rivalry occasionally got the better of him, but it was all part of growing up in a household where football was never far away. ‘It was chaotic,' he says with a smile. 'We would make too much noise in the house, but it was good.' It was Pennie's brothers who sparked his interest in football, and his first memory of kicking a ball around is as a four-year-old in a concrete courtyard outside his home. While not the most storied introduction to the beautiful game, it was the start of a journey that has shaped many chapters of Pennie’s life. It started at grassroots level, with Pennie playing Sunday League football for All Stars United. He was identified by Chelsea’s recruitment team and joined our development centre. Yet there were also sessions undertaken with Arsenal. However, the Blues proved the right fit and Pennie signed as an Under-9 with Chelsea. He says: ‘At the development centre I didn’t feel nervous – I was happy because going pro was always the ambition. I wanted to be a policeman when I was three but other than that it was always football.’ His family was delighted with the decision, and many attended his signing day at Stamford Bridge. ‘I think there were 15 people there on the day!' he recalls. 'I probably didn’t realise how big of a deal it was at the time. ‘If I could go back now and give my eight-year-old self some advice, I’d have told him to always look at the positives because there are ups and downs. I don’t like to focus on the downs.’ In the years since, Pennie has enjoyed plenty of high moments. A standout season was his Under-14 year, when he felt his performances were particularly strong and his belief in having a future in football grew. Pennie's favourite memory, though, remains winning the Under-12 Truce Cup in 2021. He scored three goals in five matches despite not yet having moved into an attacking role. 'I was a centre-back when I was younger, then a right-back aged 12,' he says. 'I wasn’t a forward until I was 13 years old. During one training session before a game against Southampton, I played up front and couldn’t stop scoring. ‘I found out I might be playing as a striker, but I didn’t want to because I was too nervous. Kwamina Ampah was pushing me and I think he said something to the coaches. I started up front against Southampton that weekend and we won 5-1. I scored four and ever since I’ve been a forward.’ Having moved into digs close to our training ground at 14 years old, Cobham has become Pennie’s home. Much of his development has come within the club’s environment and he believes Chelsea has ‘shaped me a lot as a person and how I view the world.' There have been challenges, but Pennie used each as motivation to keep getting better. After one particularly tough match, he received the advice to ‘train how I want to play’. The message stuck and Pennie now identifies his ‘bounce back’ mentality as one of the biggest improvements in his game. His family’s influence has extended well beyond those early footballing memories. Growing up, Pennie’s mother would make the hour-and-15-minute journey from home in Lewisham to Cobham every day. That commitment has never been taken for granted. 'My parents are my heroes; they are always in a positive mood and often pray for me,' he says. 'I know they are very proud of me.’ Away from the pitch, he describes himself as peaceful, although the competitive streak developed over games of FIFA and football with his brothers remains. He now often plays padel with his Chelsea team-mates and previously enjoyed basketball and cricket before focusing on football. His ambitions continue to grow in a blue shirt. Pennie wants to improve his movement off the ball and is chasing down a personal goal target for the season. Pennie's journey has been underpinned by hard work and shaped by tough lessons. He has experienced the highs of winning and finding his place on the pitch, alongside the natural challenges and disappointments that come with life as a young player. Still just 17 years old, much more is to be written in Pennie's story. With good people around him and our Academy as a nurturing backdrop, he will not lack for inspiration in the years ahead.

news.title: Bompastor updates on Manaka Matsukubo availability
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed that Manaka Matsukubo will be available to face Liverpool on Saturday afternoon, after the Chelsea striker missed out on the squad for the UEFA Women’s Champions League win against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday. The Blues sit top of the Women’s Super League ahead of the weekend’s action, hoping to push our lead over Manchester City to four points before Andree Jeglertz’s side face Tottenham on Sunday. After grinding out a late winner against PSG thanks to Veerle Buurman’s close-range finish, Bompastor has revealed the good news that Matsukubo will be able to return to action having missed the last two games. ‘The last conversation I had with the medical team, she could train normally from Thursday and then be available for the game on Saturday,’ the Blues coach said in her pre-match press conference, held after the win against PSG. ‘I think the last time she was on the pitch with us was the Hacken game. She came in and played the last 30 minutes. She was close to scoring but the goalkeeper made a really good save. ‘You can see the quality she will bring. She probably needs time to get those connections with the team-mates. But I'm convinced having her in the squad for the game on Saturday will help - starting or maybe coming off the bench.’ With Lauren James unavailable to return before the international break, Bompastor welcomed Matsukubo’s return and stressed the importance of having a range of players available to keep up with a gruelling calendar which has seen the Blues face nine games in just five weeks. ‘Yeah, it's really important to have different profiles but also different options,’ Bompastor said. ‘When you play every three days it's really good to have different options coming from the bench or starting the game. You need to have these threats everywhere on the pitch, no matter if they are starting or coming on. ‘So yeah, the quality she has, I'm convinced she will help the team on Saturday to get something.’

news.title: Emegha: 'When the time comes, I will be ready'
news.body_en: Emmanuel Emegha speaks about his unique career path to Stamford Bridge and his hunger to succeed in west London in an exclusive interview for tomorrow’s matchday programme. After making his first appearances for Chelsea prior to the international break, the young Dutch striker is keen to show the fans what he is capable of. 'I know that, when my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy,' he tells us. 'I like it here – I’m in a room full of such talented players, it’s not normal! Before coming, I knew that I could expect a high level, but I didn’t know that it would be so crazy high. But I’m enjoying it. I’m getting better. I’m learning every single day.' Emegha began his football journey playing games in the park with his twin brother in The Hague, before representing clubs in the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria and France en route to the Premier League. The 23-year-old believes the variety of experience has served him well. 'If you go to another country, you need to adapt to the country,' he explains. 'The country will not adapt to you, and that’s what I had to learn from very young.' Patient forwards are a bit of a theme in this publication, as our Legacy feature focuses on the career of George Mills, Chelsea’s top goalscorer against Leeds United and eighth highest-scorer of all-time. The powerful frontman was not a regular at the Bridge for much of his time here, but kept plugging away and racked up a total of 125 goals for the club during the interwar years, becoming an England international along the way. We also revisit some more recent history in our Greatest Games series, taking a fresh look at our 5-0 win over Leeds in April 1984, which sealed promotion to the top flight and sent the Blues fans into ecstasy. As it’s Leeds, and minds turn to that tumultuous FA Cup final in 1970, we’ve focused on hardmen in our Five feature, while there is also everything you need to know ahead of this weekend’s fixture, plus the latest from around the club. Be sure to pick up your copy from the programme sellers around Stamford Bridge, or order online from our publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds: Key statistics and facts

The Premier League resumes this weekend after the international break with Chelsea in fifth position, two points behind Liverpool in fourth. Leeds, in ninth place, go into Matchweek 11 two points off fifth place and six from the relegation zone. Leeds United return to Stamford Bridge for the second time in 10 weeks, following our 6-3 Carabao Cup win in September. This is the 99th league meeting between Chelsea and Leeds. Chelsea are unbeaten at Stamford Bridge against Leeds United in 10 games in all competitions, winning eight and drawing two. Leeds' last win at the Bridge was in December 1999, in the Premier League, when a 2-0 victory put them top of the Premier League. The Blues finished the game with 10 men, after Frank Leboeuf was sent off on 68 minutes. Leeds did not lose either Premier League game against Chelsea last season. The last time they went three meetings unbeaten against the Blues was between November 2000 and October 2001. In last season’s corresponding game at Stamford Bridge, Joao Pedro and a Cole Palmer penalty gave the Blues a two-goal lead, but second-half strikes from Lukas Nmecha and Noah Okafor earned Leeds a draw. It was the first time they had avoided defeat at the Bridge since November 2000. news.title: Sjoeke Nusken: There is more to come from us
news.body_en: Sjoeke Nusken believes Chelsea have another level to reach despite reclaiming top spot in the Women's Super League, with the midfielder determined to build on our impressive victory over Manchester City when we face Liverpool on Saturday. The Blues moved a point clear at the summit following last weekend's 1-0 triumph at Stamford Bridge, with Sandy Baltimore's brilliant strike securing an important victory over our title rivals. But while Nusken was delighted with the result, the German international believes there is still plenty of room for improvement in Sonia Bompastor's side. 'We have so much quality in our group,' said Nusken. 'We're still not on our best level. Especially in the final third, we can improve a little more, with the crossing and finishing. But it's getting better and better every single time when we're playing together, and I think you can see it. It's still a process, so we keep going.' The midfielder also insists our approach will not change now that Chelsea are the team being chased. 'We need to win every other game, otherwise it didn't help us to win against Man City. We need to win against everyone. 'We have the Champions League as well. We have a lot of games and it's important to go from game to game.' Our next league challenge comes against Liverpool at St Helens Stadium on Saturday, and Nusken is anticipating another demanding encounter. 'Liverpool are a really good team, and it's always an intense game against them. The last couple of years it was always a tight game, and they have a lot of new good signings as well. 'We need to put our best performance on the pitch like in the last game. We need to stay strong defensively to not concede anything and hopefully score more goals up front.' Now in her fourth season at Chelsea, Nusken believes the togetherness within Bompastor's squad has been important in navigating a demanding schedule. 'We're spending so much time together and it's so much more fun when we're enjoying our time here. 'We're checking in with each other, we're asking how we are and doing a lot of things off the pitch as well, so it's really nice.' The 25-year-old has also reflected on her own development since moving to England in 2023, having grown in confidence and taken on greater responsibility. 'On the field, I think I can learn a lot from different players here. I play with so many players, different types of styles, and it's so nice to have them around me and to improve every single day. 'But I have the feeling that I'm still not finished yet. I know how far I can go, and I think there's a lot more to come.' With the Women's World Cup approaching next summer and Chelsea competing for silverware on several fronts, Nusken is determined to keep progressing. 'We have so many things we can win. We have so much talent in our squad, and I think if we can still improve, working on the small details, we have a big future ahead. 'And yeah, one trophy is still missing, and of course this is the big aim for our season.'

news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club is pleased to announce that Academy forward Andrew Pennie has signed his first professional contract with the Blues. Pennie joined Chelsea aged eight and has developed into an explosive forward with a natural eye for goal. The 17-year-old has already scored 14 goals this season across all competitions for the Under-17s and Under-18s. Last season, while still a schoolboy, Pennie featured for the Under-18s and scored vital goals against Birmingham City and West Ham United, including a stunning strike in a 3-1 victory over Birmingham at Cobham. He also made his Chelsea Cobham Next Gen debut in October 2025 when he was just 15 years old, appearing in the EFL Trophy against Walsall. He has signed the professional deal following his 17th birthday, having signed a scholarship contract back in July 2026.

news.title: Liverpool vs Chelsea Women: How to watch, kick-off time, live stream info
news.body_en: Chelsea Women head to Liverpool on Saturday looking to maintain our position at the top of the Women's Super League following last weekend's vital victory over Manchester City. The Blues moved one point clear in first place after Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike secured a 1-0 win at Stamford Bridge, extending our unbeaten start to the league campaign. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Liverpool against Chelsea Women, including the kick-off time and how to follow the action on our official channels. Chelsea Women's game against Liverpool takes place on Saturday 21 November at St Helens Stadium, with kick-off scheduled for 12.45pm UK time. The match will be shown live in the UK on Sky Sports. As always, team news, live updates and match coverage will be provided in our Chelsea Women vs Everton Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and Chelsea website. You can also follow along via Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. Chelsea remain unbeaten in the WSL this season, having won eight and drawn two of our opening 10 matches. Sonia Bompastor's side have scored 29 league goals and conceded just five, with Saturday's victory over Manchester City moving us onto 26 points. Liverpool head into the contest having returned to winning ways with an impressive 3-0 victory away to Brighton & Hove Albion last weekend. Beata Olsson scored twice and Cornelia Kapocs was also on target as the Reds ended a five-match winless run in the league. Chelsea took four points from our two WSL meetings with Liverpool last season. Alyssa Thompson's superb early strike earned us a 1-1 draw at St Helens Stadium in November, before goals from Sjoeke Nusken and Lauren James secured a 2-0 victory at Kingsmeadow in February. We also faced the Reds in the Women's League Cup quarter-finals in December, producing a stunning attacking display to win 9-1 away from home and reach the last four. It was the first time a team had scored nine goals in a knockout tie in the competition's history. The Blues are unbeaten in our last six meetings with Liverpool across all competitions, winning five and drawing one, since a 4-3 WSL defeat at Prenton Park in May 2024. Our last WSL victory at St Helens came in November 2024, when goals from Mayra Ramirez, Guro Reiten and Aggie Beever-Jones secured a 3-0 win.

news.title: Bompastor: Buurman is a 'complete player and a top talent'
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has praised Veerle Buurman's maturity and development after the young defender scored the winning goal in Chelsea's 1-0 UEFA Women's Champions League victory over Paris Saint-Germain. The Dutch international struck in the 87th minute at Plough Lane, reacting quickest inside the penalty area to secure three valuable points and extend our impressive defensive record in Europe. It was another outstanding performance from the 20-year-old, who has continued to establish herself as an important member of Bompastor's squad. 'Veerle has been performing at a really good level since January this year,' said our head coach. 'She's a top talent. She's very mature, both on and off the pitch. She reads the game well, understands the game and is really smart.' Buurman was instrumental in keeping PSG at bay, demonstrating excellent defensive awareness when the visitors threatened on the counter-attack. And Bompastor believes her impressive physical attributes, combined with her composure in possession, make her a very well-rounded defender. 'She's strong and has a lot of speed to recover the space in behind. She's strong in duels, particularly aerial duels, and wins the first contact most of the time. 'She's also really confident with the ball and brings a lot of quality to the team. Her ability on the ball helps her play with that confidence.' Despite her impressive development, Bompastor believes there is still room for Buurman to improve, particularly when it comes to maintaining such high standards consistently. 'She's a really complete player and a top talent. She's helping the team perform at a really good level right now. 'But she's still young, and we sometimes have conversations about how she can remain as consistent as possible and maintain this level of performance for as long as possible.' With another assured defensive display and a decisive goal to her name, Buurman definitely showed her growing importance to the Blues.

news.title: Classic Match | Chelsea 3-2 Leeds Utd
Buurman praises Chelsea's determination after late win
news.body_en: Veerle Buurman hailed Chelsea's determination after scoring a dramatic late winner against Paris Saint-Germain, with the defender also highlighting our defensive strength and the importance of securing a top-four finish in the UEFA Women's Champions League. The Dutch youngster struck in the 87th minute at Plough Lane, turning home from close range following a corner to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory and three valuable points. It was another memorable evening for Buurman, who was named Player of the Match for the second consecutive game after also receiving the award following Saturday's victory over Manchester City. 'Of course, it's really nice to score a goal. It's a really important three points. We fought until the end with the team, and to score the winning goal is of course something to be really proud of,' said Buurman. 'I think Lucy touched it first and then I just turned and tried to shoot!' The victory was particularly welcome following our goalless draw with Hacken last time out in Europe, with Buurman explaining how the Blues remained patient against a stubborn PSG defence. 'They went deeper so we had to play a lot out wide, there was a lot of space. In the second half, we switched the formation a little bit and we did really well with a lot of crosses. 'Corners as well, we are training a lot on them, and I'm happy to score one.' Equally pleasing for Buurman was another clean sheet, our fifth in the Champions League this season, as Chelsea continued to demonstrate impressive resilience. 'Overall as a team we're doing really well in defending. A clean sheet is really important for us as a backline. It's maybe one of the nicest things if you keep a clean sheet. 'I think it started in pre-season, how we want to defend, what we expect from the midfielders in front of us, tracking the runs.' The 20-year-old has continued to develop alongside experienced defenders including Lucy Bronze, Nathalie Bjorn and Katie McCabe, whose influence she believes has been invaluable. 'I'm learning a lot from them with their experience, but to be part of the group and learning every day and every game means a lot. 'As a defender, I really like defending, and I think if you have a backline and play next to Lucy, Katie, Nat, it's amazing to play next to so much experience.' And with Chelsea now occupying a top-four position in the league phase, Buurman is determined to secure automatic qualification for the quarter-finals and avoid the additional knockout play-off round. 'We have to focus on finishing in the top four in the Champions League. That's really important. 'You miss a round (qualifying automatically), so that will be really nice. I think that's our main objective.'

news.title: PGA Division 1 report: Manchester United 2-2 Chelsea Women Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women Under-18s drew 2-2 with Manchester United Women Under-21s in the PGA Under-21 Women’s League Division 1 on Wednesday 18 November, twice taking the lead at Carrington Training Ground. Keira Johnson put the Blues ahead inside two minutes from Zoe Ciccardini’s cross, but United levelled with a free-kick just before half-time. Leanne Champ’s side created several chances in the second half and regained the lead through substitute Carla Gardiner. United equalised again in the 89th minute with a strike from distance. The opener began with Rebekah Pierce finding captain Belle Sullivan in the centre circle. Sullivan switched play to Ciccardini on the left, and Jahmya Putman ran between two United defenders to receive the ball down the side of the penalty area. Under pressure, Putman turned and found the supporting Ciccardini, who drove towards the box and crossed for Johnson. Her first touch took her past a defender and she finished from close range. Aysia Matabaro replaced Chelsea N’Drin on 41 minutes. Four minutes later, United drew level after Sullivan conceded a free-kick around 25 yards out. The hosts’ striker lifted the ball over the wall and into the top-right corner, beyond Freya Weeks. Gardiner replaced Putman on the hour and Sullivan was booked five minutes later. The Blues went back in front on 72 minutes after Chloe Sarwie beat the first United player to press her and recovered the ball when two more closed her down. Sarwie played wide to Matabaro, who beat her defender and drove a cross towards the near post. Gardiner met it with a first-time flick of her right foot to make it 2-1. Chelsea prevented a cross from United’s left in the closing stages and Ciccardini blocked the resulting shot from the edge of the area. Stevie Sinclair’s clearance reached a United centre-back just ahead of the centre circle, and she took a touch before sending a dipping strike into the net. The Blues have seven points from our opening three Division 1 fixtures and remain unbeaten after wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland. Chelsea return to Kingsmeadow on Sunday 22 November to face Birmingham City Women Under-21s in PGA Division 1. Kick-off is at 1pm. news.title: Defender voted Star of the Match against PSG!
news.body_en: Chelsea Women secured a narrow Champions League victory over Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday evening, and Blues fans have now voted for their Star of the Match. A hard-fought game of few clear chances at either end was decided late on by Veerle Buurman, who bundled the ball in from close range after an Erin Cuthbert corner caused chaos in the Paris defence. The 1-0 victory means we are still yet to concede in this season’s Champions League, and currently sit top of the the league phase table ahead of Thursday evening’s action. And it was the matchwinner Buurman who you chose as your Star of the Match for the second game running. Not only did she score the winning goal, but Buurman helped build our attacks from the back with some incisive passing, and was rock solid once again in snuffing out the opposition’s threat. She received a huge 74 per cent of the votes cast, with former PSG player Sandy Baltimore way behind in second with nine per cent.

news.title: Ibrahim Rabbaj named in Morocco squad for Under-17 World Cup
news.body_en: Ibrahim Rabbaj has been selected in Morocco's squad for the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, with the Chelsea forward set to represent his country at the tournament in Qatar. The 17-year-old is one of 21 players included by Morocco head coach Ahmed Kantari for the competition, which gets underway today. news.title: Henderson details how Blues are working to build the 'best version of ourselves'
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson says he and the other Chelsea players who remained at Cobham during the international break have been working hard to build the rhythm needed to compete at our best in every Premier League fixture. While several members of the Blues squad have been away representing their countries over the past ten days, Henderson is one of those who remained at our training base to work with Xabi Alonso. Before this pause in the domestic calendar, Henderson and his fellow Blues recorded a run of three wins from four Premier League fixtures. But we went into the break on a disappointing note, with Alonso's side suffering a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland. We return to Premier League action this weekend by hosting Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. The fixture begins a busy run over winter, during which the Blues are hoping to put our inconsistencies behind us to mount a sustained assault on the top four. ‘I think there’ve been some good things, but things that we can improve on, of course,’ said Henderson, using this pause to reflect on the 2026/27 season so far. ‘A little bit of inconsistency, but that's what we're trying to get better and improve on, trying to be more consistent every day, in training and obviously in the games, to get the best performances that we can achieve as a team and be the best version of ourselves. ‘So we'll continue to work and hopefully throughout the course of the season, and the longer the season goes on, we can find more consistency and more rhythm with our performances. ‘The important thing is not looking too far ahead. There's a long way to go in the season, a lot of points, a lot of games to play. So it's just about focusing on the next one at the minute. ‘I think we've shown some good things, but things that we need to improve on. So it's about taking it game by game, showing that we can compete in every single game and ensure that consistency. When we do that, then the results will take care of themselves.’ The 36-year-old is likely to play an important role in that push, on and off the pitch. He is one of the most experienced members of Alonso’s squad and is embracing his role as a dressing room leader despite being in his debut campaign at the Bridge. ‘I think it's important to use the experience that you've had in your career, not just when I was at Liverpool, but at other clubs that I've been at,’ he added. ‘I've been abroad and come back, so I've had a lot of different experiences that I can try and help in certain situations for the team. ‘But ultimately, at the same time, I just want to focus on playing football, playing well, training well, and if I do that then that's the biggest help I can show for the team. ‘I'm a little bit older compared to some, but I just try to be myself and try to help other people around me, whether that's in training or in games, and just do what I've done for a long time: be a good team-mate, try to help other people and try to perform to the best of my ability to help the team. ‘There's a good group of lads. I just try to be myself and lead by example as much as possible to help everybody around me in the team. But there are a lot of other players that lead by example, and it's about getting the best out of everyone, creating a good culture within the team and working hard every day. ‘I think we're on the right path and we just need to continue on that road.’ The next twist on that road which must be negotiated is a home game against old rivals Leeds. It is a challenge that Henderson knows will require the Blues to be at our best, with our opponents just two points behind us in the Premier League table. ‘It will be a very tough game against a very good team. I think they've been very good this season again. They have some really good players and are very difficult to play against, so I'm expecting a really tough game. ‘I suppose every game in the Premier League is tough, but Leeds are a very good team, so we have to be at our very best if we want to win. 'We had a bad result before the last international break and responded well, so we'll be looking to do the same again. It's important to train well this week and get ready for a big game on Saturday.’

news.title: Jordan Henderson interview
Walsh outlines importance of Blues' competitive mentality after PSG win
news.body_en: Keira Walsh believes Chelsea's squad depth is proving crucial during a demanding run of fixtures, with the midfielder praising the impact of our substitutes in Wednesday's hard-fought victory over Paris Saint-Germain. The Blues had to work for all three points at Plough Lane in our latest Champions League fixture; we had to stay patient to break down a determined PSG defence before Veerle Buurman's 87th-minute winner secured an important victory. And Walsh highlighted the contributions of Erin Cuthbert and Maika Hamano, who were introduced together on the hour and injected fresh energy into our attacking play. 'It's been a tough period and a lot of players have played different positions; there have been a lot of rotations,' said Walsh. 'Maika and Erin made a massive difference; they brought intensity and created a lot for us at the end.' 'That's the really good thing about being at Chelsea, we've got a really competitive squad and we can win these games.' Cuthbert was particularly influential in the closing stages, delivering several dangerous corners before her late set-piece eventually led to Buurman's winner. The victory was far from straightforward, with PSG's organised defensive shape frustrating the Blues for much of the evening. However, Walsh believes the determination from Sonia Bompastor's side to keep pushing and force the breakthrough could prove significant in the race for automatic quarter-final qualification. She said: 'It was a massive win. It was a tough game for us tonight; they defended really well and were aggressive. 'It was a difficult game physically but, obviously, we left it late, and to get the win was really important. And hopefully it will push us on into the top four.' While Chelsea had to remain patient in attack, our defensive resilience was again evident as Hannah Hampton recorded another clean sheet. The Blues have now kept five consecutive clean sheets in this season's league phase, an impressive achievement which Walsh believes reflects the emphasis placed on defensive discipline throughout the squad. 'I think our defence, whoever plays there, is really solid and that [keeping clean sheets] is something we're really concentrating on this year compared to last season. 'If you keep clean sheets, it really helps and if you're not scoring a lot of goals, it can help you still get these wins.'

news.title: 'Everyone is working really hard not to concede'
'I was delighted for Veerle'
Bompastor: Everyone in the team loves to defend
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor praised her Chelsea side's commitment to defending as another clean sheet helped the Blues secure a hard-fought 1-0 UEFA Women's Champions League win over Paris Saint-Germain. Veerle Buurman's 87th-minute winner earned us three vital points at Plough Lane, but our head coach was equally encouraged by the determination shown without the ball as Chelsea recorded a sixth successive European clean sheet. 'What I'm really pleased about right now is that everyone in the team loves to defend,' Bompastor said. 'We don't want to concede goals and we have a lot of quality in doing that as a team, but also some really good individuals who can defend our goal.' Bompastor believes that shared responsibility is essential to competing for silverware, particularly against opponents capable of punishing the smallest lapse. 'It's important not to concede many goals, especially when you want to go far in every competition. My job is to make sure we find the right balance between being strong defensively and creating chances and scoring goals.' That balance was tested against a PSG side who sat deep, proved difficult to break down for much of the evening, and consistently tried to his us on the counter-attack. 'I knew coming into this game, having watched a lot of PSG's previous matches, that it would be difficult,' Bompastor explained. 'They were very compact, happy to defend and protect the central areas really well. We created more chances in the second half and I think, in the end, we deserved to win.' The breakthrough eventually arrived from a corner, with Buurman turning the ball home after Bompastor's substitutions had helped Chelsea build greater attacking momentum. The victory was also another example of the flexibility within her squad, with the Blues switching between defensive systems despite a demanding fixture schedule and several injury absences. 'I think you could see tonight that we defended with both a back three and a back four, and the players still showed that confidence,' she said. The Blues head coach stressed that keeping everyone aligned in different roles takes work, but believes healthy competition is helping to drive standards higher. 'It's also about the quality of the players on the pitch. Right now, a lot of them are performing at a really good level. The competition for places in our backline is really high, which is good for us, and we need to keep that going.' For Bompastor, our late winner was a reward for perseverance, with Chelsea finding the decisive moment without compromising the defensive quality that has become a hallmark of our European campaign. 'Sometimes in football you need to find a way to win, and tonight's result was really important for us.'

news.title: UWCL Highlights: Chelsea Women 1-0 PSG Women
UWCL Extended Highlights: Chelsea Women 1-0 PSG Women
Match report: Chelsea Women 1-0 Paris Saint-Germain
news.body_en: Veerle Buurman's late winner secured a precious 1-0 victory over Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, lifting Chelsea top of the UEFA Women's Champions League league phase table with one match remaining. The Blues dominated possession but found it tough to convert chances against a disciplined PSG backline, but Buurman struck from close range following an 87th-minute corner. Sjoeke Nusken had been denied moments earlier by a magnificent save from Katarzyna Kiedrzynek, whose performance kept PSG level for much of the evening. It was another hard-earned victory for Sonia Bompastor's side, who maintained our unbeaten start to the campaign and recorded a fifth successive clean sheet in the Champions League. The result was significant after two goalless draws with Lyon and Hacken had left us needing a strong finish to the league phase. The Blues had won both European home fixtures this season, but PSG provided a different examination of our attacking patience. Bompastor made three alterations from Saturday's 1-0 Women's Super League victory over Manchester City. Nathalie Bjorn captained the Blues in place of Lucy Bronze, while Buurman replaced Kadeisha Buchanan and Aggie Beever-Jones came in for the injured Melvine Malard. The Blues quickly established control of the contest but found PSG's organised defensive shape difficult to break down. Potter had our first presentable opening in the 10th minute, meeting a corner with a free header but directing her effort wide. PSG suffered an early setback when defender Isabela was forced off injured in the 15th minute, with Olga Carmona replacing her. The visitors nevertheless remained dangerous on the break. Merveille Kanjinga offered their most persistent attacking threat down the right, demanding strong defending from Katie McCabe and the Chelsea backline. At the other end, Beever-Jones found space to meet a delivery with her head but could not direct it toward goal as clear openings remained scarce. Our best first-half opportunity arrived just before the interval. Baltimore's effort was kept out by Kiedrzynek, with Thompson reacting to the rebound but unable to force the loose ball home. Although our midfielders found space to collect the ball, PSG kept numbers behind it and protected the central areas. Bompastor's side were forced into wide deliveries, with Beever-Jones often crowded out before she could turn towards goal. Despite enjoying the majority of possession and registering seven attempts before the break, Chelsea went into half-time without making the breakthrough. PSG, meanwhile, had not forced Hannah Hampton into a save. The visitors offered more attacking ambition after the restart, and Hampton was finally called upon in the 53rd minute when Kanjinga drove towards goal and tested her at the near post. Buurman and Bjorn were alert whenever PSG threatened on the counterattack, while Potter remained composed in midfield as we continued to probe for an opening. Bompastor turned to her substitutes on the hour, introducing Erin Cuthbert, Maika Hamano and Bronze for Wieke Kaptein, Thompson and McCabe. The changes gave Chelsea fresh impetus. Cuthbert's set-piece delivery caused problems for the PSG defence, with Kiedrzynek producing another important stop following a corner. Cuthbert then worked an opening on the edge of the area but was unable to get her shot away cleanly under pressure. PSG almost punished us at the other end when Tara Elimbi Gilbert lifted an effort over the bar after a threatening counterattack involving Kanjinga and 16-year-old substitute Alyssa Charlier. With Cuthbert providing urgency from midfield and sharper deliveries from set-pieces, Chelsea began to find more promising positions. The visitors remained stubborn, however, and it appeared that a single moment might decide this finely balanced encounter. Beever-Jones sent a free-kick over the crossbar before making way for Nisken in the closing stages. The German midfielder made an immediate impression, meeting a delivery with a firm header that looked destined for goal until Kiedrzynek produced an exceptional reaction save. But the resulting corner finally broke PSG's resistance. Cuthbert delivered into the crowded penalty area and, after the ball was not cleared, Buurman reacted sharply at the near post to turn it home in the 87th minute. There was still defending to do, though, and Hampton stood firm as PSG pressed for an equaliser, including a late effort from Mbock. The final whistle confirmed another clean sheet and three valuable European points after a patient and determined display that, until the end, appeared to be heading for a draw. We remain unbeaten after five league-phase matches, with our fate to be decided in the final round. We currently lead the table, with the top four advancing directly into the knockout phase. The Blues visit Liverpool in the WSL on Saturday before concluding the Champions League league phase away to OH Leuven on 16 December.
